Celebrity jeweler Alexis Bittar, who famously branded the US a 's---hole' and the American flag a symbol of aggression, headlined a high-dollar NYC fundraiser for Democratic Senate candidates.

Packaging elite donor circles inside revolutionary socialist aesthetics creates deep cynicism about genuine grassroots political reform.

Confusing the aesthetics of anti-establishment rebellion (WHAT) with actual structural empowerment of working people (WHO).

Socialist Power dynamics rely on theatrical outrage and projected disdain for the nation while quietly consolidating elite coalition power. Actors run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by using manufactured cultural crises to mask luxury status extraction.

When you map the gap between stated revolutionary ideals and elite donor reality, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Negative will forces dominate as theatrical outrage supplants genuine reform.

The Unavoidable Truth: High-dollar fundraisers for progressive candidates rely on the exact billionaire class they publicly denounce.

The Unavoidable Lie: Radical anti-establishment rhetoric changes the underlying class dynamics of elite American politics.

Revolutionary posturing from luxury designers is merely high-end brand differentiation masquerading as systemic political critique.

It hurts to see legitimate desires for a better country co-opted by wealthy trendsetters who treat national identity like a disposable fashion statement. True care builds up communities rather than tearing them down in search of applause.

Nothing says grassroots revolution quite like a $27,000-a-plate Manhattan fundraiser hosted by a celebrity jewelry designer. Sure, calling your own country a dump is a bold campaign strategy.

Democratic Senate candidates Sherrod Brown and James Talarico reportedly headlined a star-studded New York City fundraiser hosted by celebrity jewelry designer Alexis Bittar, whose recent public comments describe the United States as a "s---hole" and characterized the American flag as "a symbol of aggression."

The fundraiser, held Monday evening in Manhattan, featured contribution levels ranging from $500 to $27,000 and also listed actor Robert De Niro among the high-powered hosts, according to an invitation cited by the Washington Free Beacon.

Bittar's recent record includes a July interview during which he discussed his concerns about the country's future, while promoting a documentary centered on "reclaim[ing]" the American flag.

During the interview, Bittar questioned what Americans were doing to create "the country we want to live in" before adding: "I have three kids, and they're little, and they're growing up in this s---hole. So if we don't do something now, we're f---ed."

FIRST ON FOX: JAMES TALARICO SLAMMED FOR CALLING AMERICAN FLAG ‘COMPLICATED SYMBOL’ AHEAD OF INDEPENDENCE DAY

Alexis Bittar and actress Brooke Shields attend the Alexis Bittar NYFW & 25th Anniversary With Lucite presentation during Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Fall 2015 on February 18, 2015, in New York City. (Andrew Toth/Getty Images for Alexis Bittar)

The Free Beacon highlighted separate remarks Bittar made about the American flag while discussing the documentary, saying in an interview with Forbes in July 2025 that the American flag had become "a symbol of aggression" during President Donald Trump's political rise.

"Thinking about the new administration and what actions I can take to combat their policies. It seemed folks were in shock and experiencing malaise. But I homed in how the flag was co-opted by the right and how did the left let that happen?" he said in the interview. "It’s become such a symbol of aggression, the American flag, like ‘we're coming for you’ during Trump’s era."

Bittar has been active in progressive Democratic politics. Gothamist previously reported that he was among the donors who gave the maximum amount to support New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's transition and served on the mayor's Arts & Culture transition committee. He has also been unafraid of the "socialist" label, the Free Beacon reported.

"Hey people … it’s voting time!!! Bringing in all the Democrat Socialists!! Let’s change America…!" he said while urging people to go out and vote for various candidates in New York several weeks ago on Instagram.

Democratic Party U.S. Senate candidates Sherrod Brown, left, and James Talarico, right. (Getty Images)

Bittar also recently hosted a fundraiser for Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, while in an August Instagram video with the U.S. Senate candidate from Michigan. Bittar declared that "the traditional Democrats have one foot in the grave" and that "the revolution has begun."

TIM SCOTT GOES SCORCHED EARTH ON EL-SAYED: 'HE'S FOR HAMAS, BUT HE'S AGAINST AMERICA'

Bittar's jewelry has been worn by celebrities including Michelle Obama, Beyoncé, Lady Gaga and Rihanna, and he has built a high-profile fashion brand while also becoming increasingly active in progressive Democratic politics.
